original_title: Chiral Rh Diene NHC Complexes and Their Application in Rh-Catalyzed Cycloisomerization of Enynes
title: Putting chiral dienes and NHCs on the same rhodium
blurb: Chiral dienes and NHCs each show up constantly in transition-metal catalysis, but apparently almost nobody's put both on one Rh center at once. This makes eight neutral and four cationic Rh diene-NHC complexes to see how the two ligand types actually interact, then runs them on enyne cycloisomerization.

original_title: A Self-Marangoni-Propelled Droplet Microarray for Ultrafast Mixing and Point-of-Care Assay of Acute Myocardial Infarction Biomarkers
title: Marangoni flow does the stirring on a heart-attack biomarker chip
blurb: A droplet microarray patterned with a hydrophobic background, superhydrophilic rings, and hydrophilic cores keeps water replenishing at each droplet's edge, which sets up surface tension gradients that drive their own 3D convection. That self-stirring is what fixes the usual droplet-array problem, poor mixing and uneven signal, for point-of-care detection of acute MI biomarkers.

original_title: Through-space conductive pathways for polyoxometalate electronics
title: Polyoxometalates that conduct without touching
blurb: Assembling quasi-aromatic clusters into a 3D network creates charge-transport pathways through space rather than through bonds, turning normally insulating polyoxometalates into intrinsic molecular conductors.

original_title: Electron‐Donating Aminosilane Bridging Enables General Access to Full‐Color Aqueous Phosphorescent Nanospheres
title: One recipe for full-color glow-in-water nanoparticles
blurb: An in-situ silanization platform uses electron-donating aminosilanes as a bridge to lock organic precursors into a silica matrix, producing monodisperse, size-tunable (10-320 nm) phosphorescent nanoparticles that work in water and afterglow anywhere from blue-purple to red. The pitch is generality: one bridging chemistry instead of a bespoke recipe per color.

original_title: Alpha particle therapy in glioblastoma: emerging biomarkers, mechanisms of response, and translational opportunities.
title: The state of alpha therapy for glioblastoma
blurb: A review rounding up where alpha particle therapy for glioblastoma stands: emerging biomarkers, what's known about why some tumors respond, and where the translational opportunities are. No new data of its own, it's a survey of the field.

original_title: Extracellular vesicles in targeted drug delivery: from biological functions to surface engineering
title: Dressing up exosomes to hit the right cells
blurb: A review of surface engineering approaches for extracellular vesicles as drug carriers. The case for EVs is that they already do intercellular delivery naturally, which gives them built-in targeting and a safety profile that synthetic nanoparticles have to work a lot harder for.

original_title: Pressure‐Induced Single‐Molecule Deformation Enables 208‐Fold Photoluminescence‐Intensity Enhancement in Zero‐Dimensional Copper Iodide Hybrids
title: Squeeze a copper iodide crystal, get 208x the glow
blurb: Pressure-induced emission enhancement in metal halides has been observed for a while without anyone pinning down the molecular cause. Here it's isolated to single-molecule deformation, shown by tuning the alkyl chain length on phosphonium cations across a series of 0D copper iodide hybrids, with one packing mode delivering a 208-fold jump in photoluminescence under pressure.

original_title: Harnessing endogenous carbon monoxide for cancer-selective drug synthesis
title: Building the drug out of the tumor's own carbon monoxide
blurb: Cancer cells run hot on endogenous CO, and this turns that into a feedstock: an albumin-based system does transition-metal-mediated synthesis directly at the tumor site, engineered specifically to survive the glutathione that normally kills these catalysts fast inside cells.

original_title: Closed-loop optimization in an industrial R&D lab
title: A closed-loop reaction optimizer built to actually stay in production
blurb: An autonomous closed-loop optimization system, hardware and software, deployed inside an industrial R&D lab and built to run across multiple reaction types rather than being tuned to one process and retired as a demo.

original_title: Semi-prep of peptides on analytical HPLC
title: Semi-prep of peptides on analytical HPLC
blurb: Hi everyone, I'm currently trying to purify bicylic peptides of 2.5 kDa made by spps for downstream testing in biological assays. For this I really only need a few mg of each compound (maybe 10+ because my PI wants me to characterize them by NMR). The problem is, our lab only has an old unreliable semiprep system that goes up to 9 ml/min with a MN C18 Htec 5 um 100 Å 250/21 column installed. I do not get reproducible runs out of that system and i can't seem to be able to separate out all deletions and other isomers etc. Our lab has access to a few analytical HPLCs (Chromaster Hitachi/VWR) and

original_title: What wonders are left to unlock using protein de novo design?
title: What wonders are left to unlock using protein de novo design?
blurb: I have a background in structure biology. We use mutations to optimise enzyme activity or even, conformational changes. I find that it's all about engineering functions because the uphill task of engineering proteins is now done. But now I am interested in understanding which frontiers are left to be scaled?

original_title: A Ruthenium(CAAC-5) Olefin Metathesis Catalyst for Bioconjugation.
title: A CAAC-ruthenium catalyst for metathesis on biomolecules
blurb: A new ruthenium olefin metathesis catalyst built around a CAAC-5 ligand, aimed squarely at bioconjugation work rather than general synthesis.

original_title: WuXi XDC Achieves GMP Release for Singapore Bioconjugate Manufacturing Site - BioPharma APAC
title: WuXi XDC's Singapore site clears GMP for bioconjugates
blurb: GMP release for WuXi XDC's Singapore bioconjugate manufacturing site, adding capacity to their ADC contract-manufacturing business. Standard capacity-expansion news, mostly useful as a supply signal for the ADC pipeline crowding in behind it.

original_title: Acylals Derived from Acrylic Anhydride as Latent Anhydride Crosslinkers for Catalyst-Free Vitrimers
title: Anhydride crosslinks that only wake up when you heat them
blurb: Acylals made from acrylic anhydride and aromatic aldehydes sit dormant in a polymer network until heat treatment converts them into real dynamic anhydride crosslinks. Small-molecule tests show the acylals themselves can exchange too, just slower and via a dissociative path, while the liberated anhydrides swap rapidly. All catalyst-free, and the latency is the actual trick: you get to process the polymer before it turns into a vitrimer.

original_title: Targeted alpha therapy for recurrent high-grade glioma with [²²⁵Ac]-PSMA: a new theranostic approach.
title: Ac-225-PSMA alpha therapy for glioma that keeps recurring
blurb: A targeted alpha therapy approach using actinium-225-PSMA in recurrent high-grade glioma, framed as a new theranostic option. PSMA's usually a prostate marker, so repurposing it here is the interesting part.
venue: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

original_title: NovAccel Expands U.S. Presence to Advance Global Actinium-225 Supply - Yahoo Finance
title: NovAccel plants a US flag to grow actinium-225 supply
blurb: NovAccel is expanding its US presence specifically to scale up global Ac-225 supply, the isotope every alpha-therapy program is quietly rationing. Another entrant chasing the same bottleneck, which says something about how tight supply actually is.

original_title: Macrophage-Targeted Quantum Dots with Short-Wave Infrared Emission for In Vivo Breast Cancer Imaging
title: SWIR quantum dots that go straight for tumor macrophages
blurb: Dextran-coated quantum dots tuned to short-wave infrared emission, built to selectively light up tumor-associated macrophages in vivo for breast cancer imaging. The pitch is ditching radioactive tracers and expensive equipment for a fluorescence readout with real depth and contrast.

original_title: Development of Blue-to-Near-Infrared rTCO-Caged Fluorogenic Probes for Click-to-Release Monitoring.
title: rTCO-caged dyes that only light up after you click them open
blurb: Fluorogenic probes caged with ring-strained trans-cyclooctene, tuned across blue to near-infrared emission, built to monitor click-to-release chemistry as it happens.

original_title: Red light-responsive bioorthogonal chemistry enabled on-demand prodrug activation for cancer therapy.
title: Red light as the trigger for switching on a prodrug
blurb: Bioorthogonal chemistry driven by red light, used to activate a prodrug on demand for cancer therapy, trading UV's shallow tissue penetration for a wavelength that actually reaches a tumor.

original_title: Development of galectin-3 targeted radioimmunoligands for cancer theranostics.
title: Galectin-3 gets its own radioimmunoligand for theranostics
blurb: Radioimmunoligands targeting galectin-3, developed as a theranostic pair for cancer imaging and treatment. A less crowded target than the usual PSMA/SSTR lineup, so worth watching where it ends up being used.

original_title: Fine-tuning thiosemicarbazones with heterocyclic substituents: identification of styryl-dependent cysteine reactivity and potent anti-cancer activity
title: Styryl groups turn thiosemicarbazones into cysteine-reactive anti-cancer leads
blurb: New PPP4HAT-targeting thiosemicarbazone analogues with improved solubility and potency, where the SAR traces the cysteine reactivity specifically to styryl substituents reacting via Michael addition. That covalent hit is presumably doing the anti-cancer work, not just target binding.

original_title: Development of Blue‐to‐Near‐Infrared rTCO–Caged Fluorogenic Probes for Click‐to‐Release Monitoring
title: Click-to-release probes that light up from blue to near-infrared
blurb: Twelve TCO-caged fluorogenic probes, eleven of them new, built to switch on with a sulfonated tetrazine trigger, spanning blue through near-infrared. They ran direct caging, self-immolative linkers, and covalent assembly head to head in live cells to see which turns on fastest and cleanest.

original_title: FDA Approves Curium’s Bexlutry (Lutetium Lu 177) for SSTR-Positive Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors - Oncodaily
title: Curium's Lu-177 drug clears the FDA
blurb: Bexlutry, Curium's lutetium Lu-177 therapy, just got FDA approval for SSTR-positive gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. Another radioligand therapy cleared for the NET indication.

original_title: Enzyme-mediated crosslinking of silk fibroin/ N-acetylcysteine-modified chitosan/hydroxyapatite hydrogel composites for subchondral bone regeneration.
title: An enzyme-crosslinked hydrogel aimed at subchondral bone
blurb: Silk fibroin, N-acetylcysteine-modified chitosan, and hydroxyapatite crosslinked enzymatically into a composite hydrogel for regenerating subchondral bone.

original_title: Leveraging Iodomethylboronic Ester Reactivity to Access Late-Stage Dehydroalanine and Dehydrovaline onto Peptides in Water
title: Turning cysteine into dehydroalanine with a boronic ester, in water
blurb: A commercially available iodomethylboronic pinacol ester bis-alkylates cysteine and penicillamine residues in peptides, converting them cleanly to dehydroalanine or dehydrovaline right in PBS. That reactive alkene handle then lets them hang thiol-bearing cargo off the peptide, a shortcut to post-translational modification mimetics without redesigning the whole synthesis.

original_title: Design rules for bioorthogonal glycan-based tools
title: A design guide for bioorthogonal glycan labeling
blurb: A review tracking metabolic glycan labeling from its early biochemical roots to the current chemical toolkit, and what each generation of methods actually taught us about glycan biosynthesis along the way.

original_title: Native Chemical Ligation-Driven Formation of Hyaluronic Acid-Based Injectable Hydrogels
title: Native chemical ligation as the crosslinker for an injectable HA gel
blurb: High-molecular-weight hyaluronic acid carrying a glycinyl thioester meets a bis-cysteine peptide crosslinker, and native chemical ligation stitches the two into an injectable hydrogel under physiological conditions. Hits the standard checklist, cytocompatible, injectable, tunable rheology, without a metal catalyst or UV cure.

original_title: Telix buys ITM for $1.65B in ‘supercritical’ radiopharma M&A - BioSpace
title: Telix drops $1.65B on ITM
blurb: Telix is buying ITM for $1.65 billion, a deal already being billed as 'supercritical' for radiopharma M&A. Consolidation in a field that's suddenly flush with cash.

original_title: Telix buys ITM in bid to create a ‘radiopharmaceutical powerhouse’ - BioPharma Dive
title: Telix's ITM buy is about scale, not just a pipeline add-on
blurb: Same Telix-ITM deal, but the framing here is building a full radiopharmaceutical powerhouse rather than bolting on another asset. Whether the combined company can execute at that scale is the open part.

original_title: A Synergistic Approach Using a ROS-Responsive Lipid-Based Prodrug for Liposomal Delivery of Doxorubicin
title: Doxorubicin gets a ROS-triggered prodrug leash inside a liposome
blurb: Prodrug design and liposomal encapsulation each patch some of doxorubicin's toxicity and biodistribution problems while introducing their own, so this stacks both: a ROS-responsive lipid prodrug packaged into a liposome for triggered intracellular release. Combining two delivery tricks to cover each one's blind spot also means two sets of failure modes to sort through.

original_title: Beyond Tumor Accumulation: Molecularly Targeted and Activatable Photoacoustic Contrast Agents
title: Photoacoustic contrast agents need more than just piling up in the tumor
blurb: A review arguing that a photoacoustic contrast agent's value isn't just how much accumulates in the tumor but the target-to-background contrast it generates, and lays out the two routes to that: molecularly targeted probes that stick via biological recognition, and activatable probes that switch on once they get there.

original_title: Radiopharmaceutical Companies Telix, ITM Merge in $1.65B Deal - GenomeWeb
title: Two radiopharma players decide to become one, for $1.65B
blurb: Telix and ITM are merging in a $1.65 billion deal, folding two companies both chasing the same radioligand therapy market into one.

original_title: Design, synthesis and biological evaluation of a series of new, potent FLT3 PROTAC degraders with rigid linkers
title: New FLT3 PROTACs swap the floppy linker for a rigid one
blurb: A new series of FLT3-degrading PROTACs built with rigid linkers instead of the usual flexible chains, designed and evaluated for potency.

original_title: Head-to-head comparison of [(18)F]AlF-NOTA-JR11 PET/MR and [(68)Ga]Ga-DOTA-TATE PET/CT in patients with neuroendocrine tumors.
title: Two NET tracers, put head-to-head
blurb: A direct comparison of [18F]AlF-NOTA-JR11 PET/MR against [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-TATE PET/CT in neuroendocrine tumor patients, pitting the newer fluorine-18 antagonist tracer against the somatostatin-analog standard it'd have to replace.
venue: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

original_title: Photoinduced Decarboxylative Radioiodination of (Hetero)aryl Carboxylic Acids
title: Radioiodination that skips the usual detour
blurb: A photoinduced, Cu(II)-mediated method swaps carboxylic acids directly for radioactive iodine, with broad substrate scope and good functional group tolerance. It works late-stage on complex bioactive molecules too, which is the part that actually matters for making radiopharmaceuticals.

original_title: Novartis makes latest radioligand bet with $900M BoomRay deal - FirstWord Pharma
title: Novartis adds another radioligand bet, BoomRay for $900M
blurb: Novartis licenses BoomRay's radioligand asset for $900 million, the latest in its ongoing radiopharma buying spree.

original_title: Catalytic C(sp2)–F Bond Gallylation via Dynamic Ni–Ga Cooperativity
title: Turning C–F bonds into C–Ga bonds without a supporting ligand in sight
blurb: An unsupported Ni-Ga bimetallic system converts aryl C–F bonds into C–Ga bonds, switching between bimetallic and trimetallic modes to get through the catalytic cycle. Cooperative catalysis usually needs a ligand scaffold to hold the two metals together; this one doesn't.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: On-Surface Heptagon Contraction Enables Rearrangement Driven Selective C–C Coupling
title: A heptagon that rearranges itself before it bonds
blurb: On-surface synthesis on Au(111) where a seven-membered ring contracts to six-plus-one before coupling, generating reactive ends without any pre-installed halogen handle. A dibromotropone model confirms the contraction actually happens, useful for frameworks too stubborn to halogenate in solution.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Rh(III)-Catalyzed [4 + 2] Spiroannulation of 2-Phenylbenzimidazoles with Isomerizable 3-Methylmaleimides: Synthesis of Spiro-Fused Benzimidazoisoquinoline Succinimides
title: Rh(III) builds spiro succinimides via a [4+2] cascade
blurb: A Rh(III)-catalyzed [4+2] cyclization of 2-phenylbenzimidazoles with 3-methylmaleimides makes spiro-fused benzimidazoisoquinoline succinimides, running through N-directed C–H activation, migratory insertion of an isomerized maleimide into the Rh–C bond, then reductive elimination.

original_title: Novartis licenses BoomRay radioligand asset for $900M - european-biotechnology.com
title: BoomRay's radioligand asset is now Novartis's, for $900M
blurb: Novartis licenses the radioligand program from BoomRay for $900 million, another notch in its radioligand acquisition run.

original_title: Direct Visualization of a Hydroperoxy Intermediate in Fluorescent Protein Chromophore Maturation in PAmCherry1
title: Caught the peroxide mid-maturation in a fluorescent protein
blurb: Serial femtosecond crystallography on PAmCherry1 before photoactivation catches a covalently bound hydroperoxy group sitting on the chromophore's Cα at 73% occupancy, a step in oxidative chromophore maturation nobody had directly seen before the double bond forms.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: An in vitro comparative study of cefiderocol, siderophore-aztreonam and siderophore-daptomycin conjugates against select gram-negative bacteria
title: Cefiderocol vs two experimental siderophore conjugates, head to head
blurb: An in vitro comparison of cefiderocol against experimental siderophore-aztreonam and siderophore-daptomycin conjugates on select gram-negative bacteria. The daptomycin one is the odd inclusion, since daptomycin normally can't touch gram-negatives, so smuggling it in via a siderophore is the interesting bit here.

original_title: Nanomicelles self-assembled using cyclosporine A-hyaluronic acid conjugates for dry eye disease treatment.
title: A hyaluronic acid trick for getting cyclosporine into dry eyes
blurb: Cyclosporine A conjugated to hyaluronic acid self-assembles into nanomicelles aimed at dry eye disease. Hyaluronic acid already lubricates the eye on its own, so the carrier isn't just dead weight for delivery.

original_title: Ambient light drives verteporfin-induced protein cross-linking during standard laboratory sample processing.
title: Your lab's ceiling lights might be wrecking your verteporfin samples
blurb: Verteporfin cross-links proteins under plain ambient light, not just the light meant to activate it, so standard bench handling can quietly generate artifacts in anything using it. Worth wondering how many past results that's already touched.

original_title: Visible-light-induced trifluoroacetylation reaction of electron-deficient nitrogen heterocycles
title: Trifluoroacetyl groups onto tricky heterocycles, no catalyst required
blurb: Direct C-H trifluoroacetylation of electron-deficient N-heterocycles has been a pain because the trifluoroacetyl radical is unstable and the electronics run backwards for these substrates. This one just uses visible light: no pre-functionalization, no metal catalyst, no extra additives.

original_title: Simple and Efficient Automated Radiosynthesis of 1‐[ 18 F]‐IPA Using Solid‐Phase Extraction Cartridges Purification
title: A GMP-ready shortcut for making the PET tracer 1-[18F]-IPA
blurb: An automated synthesis of 1-[18F]-IPA, a fluorinated indole-3-propionic acid analogue being explored as a PET tracer for pancreatic cancer, swaps in cartridge-based purification for the usual workup. Built to GMP spec and meets release criteria for human use, so this is aimed at the clinic, not just a proof of concept.
venue: Journal of Labelled Compounds and Radiopharmaceuticals

original_title: Intramolecular Dearomative [2 + 2] Cycloadditions of (Hetero)arenes Utilizing an Energy-Transfer Organic Photocatalyst
title: Dearomatizing arenes with a phenothiazine photocatalyst
blurb: An energy-transfer photocatalyst built from phenothiazine, not a metal complex, drives intramolecular dearomative [2+2] cycloadditions on naphthamides and benzoheterocycles under mild conditions to build complex polycyclic scaffolds. DFT backs the proposed mechanism, and at least the catalyst itself is easy to make.

original_title: Electrochemical Sequential Cross-Dehydrogenative Coupling for the Chemoselective Synthesis of Bis(arylthio)-Substituted Biphenyl Diamines
title: Electrochemistry sequences C-C then C-S bonds in one pot, no oxidant
blurb: C-C and C-S coupling usually fight each other in the same pot since thiols overoxidize so easily. This electrochemical method skips the oxidant and the metal catalyst entirely, using oxidation-potential differences and controlled current to run C(sp2)-H/C(sp2)-H coupling first, then C(sp2)-H/S-H coupling, to build bis(arylthio)biphenylenediamines. The authors say it's a first.

original_title: Ligand-Shell-Enabled Silver Catalysis on Gold Nanoclusters for the Straightforward Synthesis of β-Naphthol Ethers from Alkynes
title: Gold nanoclusters lend their chloride to silver catalysis
blurb: Cationic gold usually has to be pre-made before it'll do this kind of pi-acid chemistry, but here chloride-containing gold nanoclusters form Au-Cl-Ag intermediates inside their own ligand shells, and the actual catalysis happens at the silver site. That combination isomerizes and cyclizes alkynes straight into naphthalene rings for beta-naphthol ethers.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Skeletal Editing of Polarized σ-Bonds via Formal Single-Carbon Insertion
title: Carbenes as a one-carbon insertion tool for skeletal editing
blurb: A rundown of carbene-mediated single-carbon insertion into polarized sigma bonds, past the usual X-H insertion and cyclopropanation tricks, for ring expansion and skeletal reconstruction. Reads like a survey of where the field has landed rather than a new result.

original_title: Radiopharmaceutical Dealmaking Continues With Telix’s $1.65B ITM Acquisition - MedCity News
title: Telix buys ITM for $1.65B, radiopharma consolidation keeps rolling
blurb: Telix is acquiring ITM for $1.65 billion, the latest entry in a run of radiopharmaceutical dealmaking. Another sign the money is betting big on isotopes right now.

original_title: De Novo Design and Structural Optimization of Mn(salen)‐Based Artificial Metalloenzymes for Asymmetric Sulfoxidation
title: De novo proteins beat the free catalyst at asymmetric sulfoxidation
blurb: Computationally designed proteins wrap a Mn(salen) complex instead of a natural cofactor, which is the whole point of building the scaffold from scratch rather than repurposing an existing protein pocket. The engineered version outperforms the free cofactor outright, up to 45% better by their own numbers.

original_title: Lattice-Confined Rh Single Atoms in SrTiO3 Enable Leaching-Resistant and Durable Heterogeneous Hydroformylation
title: Locking Rh atoms into SrTiO3 so they stop leaching out
blurb: Single Rh atoms get embedded in the perovskite lattice instead of sitting exposed on a surface, so the CO that normally carbonylates and strips Rh off a catalyst can't pull it loose. Heterogeneous Rh hydroformylation usually trades activity for stability; this one is pitched as keeping both.

original_title: Nickel-Catalyzed Carbonylative Synthesis of 1,6-Diketones from Cycloalkylsilyl Peroxides and Arylboronic Acids
title: Nickel strings silyl peroxides and boronic acids into 1,6-diketones
blurb: Cycloalkylsilyl peroxides act as carbonyl-bearing alkyl radicals, formic acid stands in as a safe CO source, and nickel couples them with arylboronic acids to give 1,6-diketones in good yield with decent functional group tolerance. Formic acid as the CO source beats hauling around a gas cylinder.

original_title: Enantioselective Synthesis of Carbazole-Thioisatin Spirocycles via NHC-Catalyzed Remote N–H Activation
title: NHC catalysis spins carbazoles and thioisatins into chiral spirocycles
blurb: An NHC catalyst turns 1-formylcarbazoles into aza-ortho-quinone methides that annulate with thioisatins, an electrophile barely used in asymmetric NHC catalysis. Yields top out around 76%, but the enantiomeric ratios reach 98:2, and ordinary isatins work in the same protocol.

original_title: Fine Tuning of Catalyst Active Sites to Access Advanced Ultrahigh‐Melting Polyolefins
title: Dialing in Hf catalyst sites for polyolefins that shrug off 200°C
blurb: Pyridylamido-Hf catalysts already handle bulky monomers like allyltrimethylsilane, producing isotactic polymer that melts at 310°C, but they stall on other sterically demanding monomers. This is about fine-tuning the active site to widen that list, not a new catalyst family.

original_title: Recyclable and Scale-Up-Compatible Ag/I-Mediated Synthesis of Aryl α-Keto Acids from Terminal Alkenes Using Dioxygen as the Terminal Oxidant
title: Silver and iodine turn styrenes into aryl α-keto acids, air does the oxidizing
blurb: Ag2O plus a recyclable iodine redox mediator converts terminal aryl alkenes straight to α-keto acids using molecular oxygen as the oxidant, in DMSO/water under a stepwise heating protocol. The recyclable mediator and scale-up compatibility are the pitch over the usual harsh, single-use routes.

original_title: Alternating Copolymerization of Arynes and Aldehydes Enabled by an N -Arylamine Initiator
title: An amine initiator makes arynes and aldehydes alternate instead of homopolymerizing
blurb: Arynes left alone just polymerize with themselves. A simple N-arylamine initiator suppresses that and forces strict alternating copolymerization with aldehydes through a Smiles-type rearrangement, regenerating a live chain end each cycle so block and cyclic polymer architectures become accessible, not just linear chains.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Synthesis of Dihydro-indolo-oxazines via a RedOx‑Neutral, Gold‑Catalyzed Hydride‑Transfer Process
title: Gold catalysis gets its hydride donor without an amine choking it
blurb: Tertiary amines are the usual hydride source for gold-catalyzed intramolecular hydride transfer, but they bind gold too tightly and stall the catalyst. Benzyl ethers work instead, and the resulting redox-neutral C-H functionalization gives a route to dihydro-indolo-oxazines.

original_title: Directed Amination as a Strategy for C–N Bond Formation by Iron Imido Complexes
title: A bigger imido ligand gets a three-coordinate iron doing C-N bond formation
blurb: Swapping in a larger, more electron-withdrawing imido group on a bis(carbene)borate iron scaffold yields a new, fully characterized iron(III) imido complex, extending a platform this group already built around low-coordinate, high-spin iron. Mostly synthesis and characterization, laying groundwork for the directed amination chemistry it's aimed at.

original_title: Nickel-Catalyzed Diastereoselective Cascade Cyclization/Cross-Coupling for the Synthesis of Dibenzazepines
title: Nickel cascades its way to dibenzazepines with total diastereocontrol
blurb: A labile ligand falls off to open a coordination site, the alkene binds, and the cyclization/cross-coupling runs through an eight- to nine-membered nickelacycle transition state, backed by DFT, giving exclusive diastereoselectivity. Broad substrate scope for a ring system that's normally a pain to build.

original_title: Future scenarios of radioligand therapy in pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas.
title: Mapping where radioligand therapy could take pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma
blurb: A look ahead at how radioligand therapy might evolve for pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas, sketching future directions rather than fresh trial results.

original_title: Liquid–Metal-Induced Metal–Support Interactions for CO2 Hydrogenation
title: Liquid indium does metal-support interaction's job without the 500°C bake
blurb: Molten indium sitting on NiO at room temperature, even down to −41°C, pulls lattice oxygen out and leaves oxygen-deficient Ni sites that activate CO2 better. Classical metal-support interaction needs a high-temperature treatment that sinters the metal and buries it in oxide, so pulling this off in liquid form at room temperature and below is the actual trick here.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Plasma multi-omics reveals molecular remodeling and prognostic biomarkers in advanced breast cancer treated with trastuzumab deruxtecan
title: Watching T-DXd rewire a breast cancer patient's blood chemistry
blurb: Paired plasma proteomics and metabolomics before and after two cycles of trastuzumab deruxtecan in 16 breast cancer patients, hunting for circulating markers of response and prognosis. Sixteen paired samples is enough to flag candidate biomarkers, not enough to trust them yet.

original_title: Symmetry-Selective Franck–Condon and Herzberg–Teller Coupling Enables Ultra-Narrow Blue Phosphorescence in Pt(II) Complexes
title: Why some Pt(II) emitters glow in a 10 nm sliver of blue
blurb: Symmetry analysis explains why certain trans-(NHC)2Pt butadiynyl complexes emit an ultra-narrow 10-14 nm blue band: C2V symmetry locks the T1→S0 transition to one axis and makes the vibronic coupling so mode-selective that nearly everything piles into the 0-0 line. Deep-blue phosphors are usually a color-purity mess, so having an actual mechanistic handle on why these aren't is the news.

original_title: Outside Front Cover: Directional Second Sphere Effect on CO 2 Activation and Reduction by Iron Porphyrin in Aprotic and Protic Media
title: Iron porphyrin's CO2 chemistry bends to which way the second sphere points
blurb: Cover story on how the direction of second-sphere interactions around an iron porphyrin catalyst controls CO2 activation and reduction, and how that plays out differently in protic versus aprotic solvents.

original_title: Access to Axially Chiral Diaryl Ethers via Catalytic Atroposelective [2+2+2] Cycloaddition of Alkynyloxybenzenes
title: Building axially chiral diaryl ethers in one shot with rhodium
blurb: A rhodium-catalyzed atroposelective [2+2+2] cycloaddition stitches phenoxyalkynes and 1,6-diynes straight into diaryl ethers carrying a C-O stereogenic axis, skipping the usual desymmetrization route and preassembled chiral building blocks, and still comes out in high yield.

original_title: Additional Reductant-Free Visible-Light-Driven Davis–Beirut-Type Reaction: Access to Indazolin-3-ones from o -Nitrobenzaldimines
title: Blue light and bromoalkanes turn nitro groups into indazolinones, no reductant needed
blurb: A visible-light Davis-Beirut variant swaps out the usual reducing agent: bromoalkanes pull double duty in a direct photochemical oxygen-atom transfer that cyclizes o-nitrobenzaldimines into indazolin-3-ones. No photocatalyst, no transition metal, no reductant, with a wide substrate scope at moderate-to-good yields.

original_title: Hydrogen‐Bond Encoding in a Structurally Minimal Cyclochiral Monomer Enables Assembly of Large Cavities Displaying Supramolecular Isomerism
title: A minimal H-bonded monomer that folds itself into fullerene-sized cages
blurb: A structurally simple monomer wired with both intra- and intermolecular hydrogen bonds locks into a cyclochiral shape and self-assembles into large, discrete capsules big enough to bind fullerenes, standing in for the usual rigid covalent scaffolds. It also turns up supramolecular isomerism, same building block, different assembled structures.

original_title: Synthesis of Conjugated Bromoenynoates via Electrophilic Bromination of Enynyl Hydrazones
title: Steering bromoenynoate geometry through 1,3-strain
blurb: Remote electrophilic bromination of enynyl hydrazone carboxylates gives densely functionalized bromoenynoates, and whether you get the Z-bromoenynoate or the E-bromodienynoate is substrate-controlled via allylic 1,3-strain, up to 80% yield at >20:1 Z/E or 96% at >20:1 E/Z. Runs at gram scale too.

original_title: Encouraging the Exploration of Nickel Catalysis in Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Processes: Lessons Learned during Catalyst Screening and Process Optimization for the Monoarylation of Ammonia
title: What catalyst screening for nickel-catalyzed ammonia arylation actually teaches you
blurb: A process-chemistry writeup on screening nickel catalysts for monoarylating ammonia, the kind of non-PGM route that's suddenly fashionable in the literature but rarely gets tried on real manufacturing processes. The underlying pitch: how many existing drug processes could've used non-PGM catalysis if it had been ready sooner.

original_title: Extending single-cell proteomics from HeLa to small primary human immune cells
title: Single-cell proteomics moves past HeLa to actual immune cells
blurb: A label-free platform pairing tightened low-input prep with an Orbitrap Astral Zoom pulls up to 7000 proteins out of a single HeLa cell at over 100 samples a day, and now it holds up on small primary human immune cells instead of just the usual immortalized workhorse line.

original_title: Sequential Strecker–Ugi, Pictet–Spengler, and Ring-Expansion Reactions for the Synthesis of the Imidazopyridine-Fused Azocinoindole Scaffold
title: Three reactions in a row build an eight-membered ring nobody keeps on the shelf
blurb: A three-component Strecker-Ugi stitches together the imidazole ring, a regioselective Pictet-Spengler closes a seven-membered azepinoindole at indole's C-4, and an ipso ring expansion pushes that up to the eight-membered azocinoindole. A genuinely new polycyclic scaffold, and it comes out regioselectively rather than as a pile of isomers.

original_title: Site-Selective C(sp3)–H Bromination via Radical Relay
title: Bromination that finds the benzylic C-H and leaves the rest alone
blurb: Just 1 mol% CoBr2 and NBS, radical relay, and better than 20:1 selectivity for benzylic over aliphatic C-H bonds. Broad substrate scope and it works late-stage on actual drug molecules and natural products, not just clean model compounds.

original_title: Coordination Behavior of Th(IV) with Tetradentate N,O-Ligands: Solvent Extraction, Complexation, and XRD Study
title: Locking down thorium with phenanthroline-diamide ligands
blurb: Solvent extraction, titration, XRD, and XAS on a series of 1,10-phenanthroline-2,9-diamide ligands show Th(IV) forming neutral ThL(NO3)4 complexes, the tetradentate N,O-ligand and four bidentate nitrates wrapped around the metal. Unglamorous coordination chemistry, but it's exactly what a thorium fuel cycle needs if separating the stuff efficiently ever becomes someone's actual job.

original_title: Electrochemical CO Reduction to n-Propanol on Cu via Dual Weakening of CO Adsorption and C≡O Bond Strength
title: Cu electrodes tuned to make propanol instead of stalling at ethanol
blurb: Anion-functionalized graphene quantum dots (OH, NH2, SO3) stuck on copper weaken both CO's grip on the surface and its C≡O bond, which pushes CO reduction toward the rare *C2 intermediate you actually need for n-propanol instead of the usual two-carbon dead end.

original_title: Efficient and Selective Low-Temperature Polypropylene Hydrogenolysis Using Zr-Doped Mixed Metal Oxides Catalysts
title: Cracking polypropylene without the platinum
blurb: Zr-doped Co/Ni-Al mixed metal oxides (CAZ, NAZ, NCZ) hydrogenolyze isotactic polypropylene down to liquid hydrocarbons at 250°C and 20 bar H2, no Ru or Pt involved. Noble-metal cost is the thing that's kept plastic hydrogenolysis from scaling, so swapping in Zr-doped base metals is the actual point here.

original_title: Telix and ITM merge in $1.65B deal poised to expand radiopharmaceutical development and manufacturing - Radiology Business
title: Telix and ITM merge in a $1.65B radiopharma bet
blurb: Telix and ITM are combining in a $1.65 billion deal meant to widen the pipeline and manufacturing muscle behind radiopharmaceuticals. Consolidation in a field that's spent years being bottlenecked on isotope supply.

original_title: Telix to Acquire ITM in $1.65 Billion Radiopharmaceutical Merger - BioPharm International
title: $1.65B buys Telix a bigger slice of radiopharma manufacturing
blurb: Telix is acquiring ITM outright for $1.65 billion, folding ITM's radiopharmaceutical manufacturing into its own pipeline. Buying the manufacturer instead of just partnering with one is a fairly blunt way to fix a supply problem.

original_title: Helicity Synchronization-Induced Kinetic Stabilization against Helix Inversion in Stapled Peptides: Effects of 310/α Block Sequence and Double-Stapling Topology
title: Achiral building blocks, but the stapled peptide still picks one helix and sticks to it
blurb: A series of doubly stapled block peptides mixing α and 3(10) helical segments, built entirely from achiral pieces, still snap into exclusively homochiral (P,P) or (M,M) helices. Neighboring segments with different geometries and hydrogen-bonding patterns are somehow still talking to each other well enough to force the whole peptide to agree on a hand, no chiral centers required.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Simultaneous Quantification of Eight Bioactive Markers Coupled With HPLC Fingerprint and Chemometric Analysis for Quality Discrimination of Saposhnikovia divaricata From Diverse Geographical Origins
title: Fingerprinting Fangfeng batches by where they actually grew
blurb: HPLC fingerprinting plus chemometrics quantifies eight bioactive markers, four chromones and four coumarins, across Saposhnikovia divaricata batches well enough to tell commercial sources apart by geographic origin. The kind of standardization TCM quality control needs given how much batch-to-batch variation is apparently out there.

original_title: Vacuum‐Induced Surface Reconstruction of Mn–Ce Oxides for Low‐Temperature Coupled Redox Catalysis
title: Baking the surface, not the bulk, into a better Mn–Ce catalyst
blurb: Vacuum annealing then a low-pressure O2 treatment pulls Mn to the near-surface of a Mn–Ce oxide while leaving the CeO2 fluorite lattice mostly intact, and that surface enrichment is what boosts the low-temperature redox catalysis. Bulk composition tuning gets all the attention normally; this is a case for just reconstructing the outermost layers instead.

original_title: Ternary-Ion Batteries
title: Batteries get a third ion to play with
blurb: Single-ion shuttling gives you energy density but chokes on multivalent kinetics, dual-ion fixes the kinetics by burning through electrolyte. This one adds a third ion so the two mechanisms cooperate instead of trading off. Whether it holds up outside the paper's own cell is the open question, but the framing at least tries to dodge a real tradeoff rather than just split the difference.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Multidirectional Colossal Polarization in a Centrosymmetric Crystal via Long-Range Ion Displacement
title: A centrosymmetric crystal that polarizes anyway
blurb: Ferroelectrics are supposed to need a noncentrosymmetric structure, but this nonpolar proton conductor delivers colossal polarization anyway, via protons dragging ions along over long range rather than any built-in asymmetry. Confirmed by ferroelectric hysteresis and thermally stimulated current, so it's not just a stray reading.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Heptafluorobutyric Acid-Induced Cross-Dehydrogenative Coupling Reactions of 1,2,4-Triazines. Part 2: p-Coupling with Arylamines
title: HFBA does the coupling, so the metal catalyst can sit this one out
blurb: Heptafluorobutyric acid drives a metal-free cross-dehydrogenative coupling that hooks 1,2,4-triazines onto arylamines, landing regioselectively at the para position under mild conditions. Works on fluorophore scaffolds like triphenylamine, carbazole, and phenothiazine, so it's aimed as much at materials chemists as drug hunters.

original_title: Cascade Spirocyclization–Difunctionalization or Rearrangement of Bicyclobutyl-Tethered Aldehyde Hydrazones via Strain Release
title: Strain release sends bicyclobutyl hydrazones down two different paths
blurb: N-halosuccinimides push bicyclobutyl-tethered aldehyde hydrazones into a spirocyclization/difunctionalization cascade, building halo-succinimide diazaspiro[3.3]heptanones. Swap in NH-sulfoximines as a third component and the same strain-release chemistry instead rearranges into halo-sulfoximine cyclobutane carboxamides. They also checked it scales up, which is more than most cascade papers bother to show.

original_title: Synthesis of 1,4-Benzoxazepines via [4 + 3] Annulation of ortho -Vinylphenols and Azaoxyallyl Cations
title: Vinylphenols plus azaoxyallyl cations build the seven-membered ring
blurb: A formal [4+3] between ortho-vinylphenols and in-situ azaoxyallyl cations, generated from alpha-halohydroxamates, assembles 1,4-benzoxazepines in one pot, no metal, just Cs2CO3 in dichloromethane at room temperature. Broad substrate scope and moderate-to-excellent yields, backed up with late-stage modification of a natural-product derivative.

original_title: Ultra-thin WS2 growth by ALD from bis(tert-butylimido)bis(dimethylamido)tungsten and 1,2-ethanedithiol and detailed surface mechanism
title: WS2 by ALD, swapping H2S for a thiol that won't kill you
blurb: Ethanedithiol stands in for H2S as the sulfur source, reacting with a tungsten imido/amido precursor to grow ultrathin WS2 through a molecular organothiolate intermediate. They chase the mechanism across wafers, nanobeads, and molecular models, and it turns out messier than a clean ALD cycle: ligand exchange, partial tungsten reduction, and some degrafting along the way.

original_title: Activating the Anomalous Jahn–Teller Effect in NASICON-Type Mixed Phosphate Cathode via Crystal Field Engineering
title: Vanadium talks the Jahn-Teller distortion into behaving
blurb: Mn3+/Mn2+ redox is the high-voltage payoff in polyanionic cathodes, but the Jahn-Teller distortion it drags along wrecks kinetics. Substituting vanadium into this NASICON phosphate/pyrophosphate cathode reconfigures that distortion and couples it to multivalent redox instead of fighting it, which is what nets the energy density and rate gains.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Synthesis of a Fully Functionalized Chasmanine AF-Ring Fragment
title: The hard ring of chasmanine, built and fully decorated
blurb: C6-oxidized C19-diterpenoid alkaloids have basically never been synthesized, and this is a route to the fully functionalized AF-ring fragment of chasmanine: a Piancatelli rearrangement builds the F ring, then a Mg-alkoxide-templated [4+2] stitches on the A ring. They also drop a bench-stable reagent for turning aldehydes straight into nitriles, useful well beyond this synthesis.

original_title: Photoinduced Trifluoromethyl‐ and Difluoromethyl‐Chalcogenation of α‐Diazo Compounds
title: Diazo compounds get their fluoroalkyl-chalcogen tag under light, not heat
blurb: A photochemical route installs trifluoromethylthio and difluoromethyl-chalcogen groups onto alpha-diazo compounds under mild, green conditions, sidestepping the harsh conditions and narrow substrate lists that usually come with making these organofluorides. Those groups matter for drugs and agrochemicals, so a milder on-ramp is the actual selling point here.

original_title: Copper-Catalyzed Formal [5 + 1] Annulation of Diynes with 1 H -Indole-2-ethanols: Construction of Tetrahydropyrano Indoles
title: A copper catalyst does a job only noble metals could do
blurb: Diynes plus indole-2-ethanols cyclize through vinyl cation intermediates into tetrahydropyrano indoles, run entirely on copper instead of the usual Pd or Au. This flavor of diyne annulation with a dinucleophile has apparently only worked with noble metals before, so getting it onto copper is the actual news here.

original_title: Unveiling the Anti‐Heavy Atom Effect in Organic Ionic Host‐Guest Phosphorescent Scintillator
title: Heavy atoms usually help scintillators, here they don't
blurb: Loading halogens onto a phosphorescent scintillator is supposed to boost X-ray response via the heavy atom effect, but this ionic host-guest system runs the opposite direction. The mechanism behind this "anti-heavy atom effect" is still murky, which is presumably why it's getting a name.

original_title: The Barriers Limiting Radiopharmaceutical Access - themedicinemaker.com
title: What's actually keeping radiopharmaceuticals from patients
blurb: A trade-press rundown of the access bottlenecks in radiopharma rather than a study. Useful for the industry framing, not the chemistry.

original_title: Single‐Atom O/S/Se Substitution at the Glycosidic Linkage in Glycopeptide Cancer Vaccines Reveals Divergent Performance
title: Swap one atom in the glycosidic bond, get a different vaccine
blurb: Swapping O, S, or Se at the glycosidic linkage of MUC1 Tn glycopeptide vaccines changes antibody recognition, ranked by SPR and backed up with MD and a second binding assay. A one-atom edit shouldn't move antigen recognition this much, but apparently it does.

original_title: Negatively Curved Nanohoops as Cut-Outs of Carbon Toroids and Schwarzites
title: Bigger cutouts of the carbon toroids nobody's actually made
blurb: Negatively curved nanohoops scaled up to 152, 228, and 304 carbons, the largest cutouts yet of the toroid and schwarzite carbon allotropes that mostly exist on paper. Two structures got solved by X-ray, and in solution they bind fullerenes, tying the synthetic pieces back to the macrostructures they're meant to mimic.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Simple and Efficient Automated Radiosynthesis of 1-[(18)F]-IPA Using Solid-Phase Extraction Cartridges Purification.
title: A cleaner automated route to 18F-IPA
blurb: Automated radiosynthesis of 1-[18F]-IPA swaps HPLC for solid-phase extraction cartridge purification, a simpler, faster cleanup step for a routine tracer.

original_title: Analysts ‘extremely bullish’ as Telix beams into Novartis’ territory with $1.6B ITM acquisition
title: Telix buys its way into Lutathera's turf for $1.6B
blurb: Telix is paying $1.65 billion upfront for ITM Isotope Technologies Munich, picking up a radioligand pipeline that competes directly with Novartis' Lutathera plus ITM's own isotope supply network. Analysts are calling themselves "extremely bullish," which is their job, but the supply network is the part that actually derisks this deal.

original_title: A Modular (1,3-Oxathiolan-2-yl)ethoxy Trigger Unlocks Activatable Probes for In Vivo Imaging of Hypobromous Acid
title: A trigger that lights up for hypobromous acid in vivo
blurb: A modular oxathiolane-ethoxy (OTE) group reacts with hypobromous acid through oxidation then beta-elimination, flipping on a fluorophore or chemiluminophore. Bolt it onto different reporters and you get a general way to track HOBr, a reactive oxygen species that's been hard to image outside a cuvette, in living animals.

original_title: Dielectric Nanolensing: How a Wavelength-Scale Lens Carries Hidden Detail into an Ordinary Microscope and What Chemistry Should Build Next
title: Squeezing more resolution out of an ordinary microscope with one extra lens
blurb: A perspective on dielectric nanolensing: drop a wavelength-scale lens into the specimen's near field and it funnels otherwise inaccessible spatial detail into a standard objective. What started as a single molecular-lens trick has grown into a whole family, microsphere, scanning, arrayed, computational, now applied to white-light nanoscopy, semiconductor metrology, living-cell optics, and substrate-free Raman. It's a review, so the "what chemistry should build next" part is the pitch, not a result.
